title: Pinning of a High-Energy Wavepacket by a Single Impurity
authors: Fartash Chalangari, Anant Vijay Varma, Joonas Keski-Rahkonen, Esa Räsänen
abstract: We demonstrate that a single repulsive impurity enhances directional confinement of a high-energy wavepacket in a finite two-dimensional lattice of quantum wells. At energies far above the interwell barriers, the impurity suppresses transverse dynamical tunneling while preserving propagation along a principal lattice axis, even as the corresponding classical regular region shrinks. Confinement is strongest at impurity amplitudes comparable to the barrier height and weakens for stronger perturbations. Spectral analysis links this nonmonotonic pinning to the wavepacket's overlap with eigenstates concentrated along the launch direction, consistent with impurity-induced variational scarring. These results show that a single local defect can control quantum propagation over distances far exceeding its own spatial extent.
summary: This work demonstrates that a single impurity can act as a quantum gate, dynamically confining a high-energy wavepacket along a preferred direction in a 2D lattice. This pinning effect is robust, persisting even when classical transport mechanisms fail. The findings connect this control to the underlying structure of the system's eigenstates, suggesting a mechanism of impurity-induced variational scarring.
main_problem: The study investigates how a single, local repulsive impurity can dynamically confine a high-energy wavepacket in a 2D quantum lattice, suppressing transverse tunneling while maintaining directional propagation.
main_result: The impurity enhances directional confinement, a phenomenon linked to impurity-induced variational scarring, persisting even when the classical regular region shrinks.
method: The analysis uses time evolution simulations (split-operator) and spectral analysis, comparing quantum probability distributions (Husimi function) against classical ensemble trajectories.
model_or_system: The system is a single particle in a finite 2D lattice of quantum wells, governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating a lattice potential and a localized Gaussian impurity potential.
key_observables: Probability $P_\alpha(t)$ in specific channels, Husimi function density, and the mean channel probability $\langle P(T) angle_\alpha$.
important_parameters: High energies far above interwell barriers; impurity strength $A/V_0$; time $T=1000$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing quantum dynamics to classical dynamics and utilizing spectral decomposition methods.
figures_summary: Figures show the contrast between classical spreading and quantum confinement due to the impurity, and plots demonstrate nonmonotonic confinement dependence on impurity strength.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the physical model and Hamiltonian, simulating wavepacket propagation, analyzing the confinement using spectral and time-averaging techniques, and finally linking the observed pinning to variational scarring.
why_interesting: The ability of a single, local defect to control quantum transport over long distances by manipulating wavepacket overlap with specific eigenstates is a key concept in understanding quantum localization and wave dynamics in engineered disordered media.
